title: acp/session-protocol — v1
description: Describes how to detect ACP stdio session status from line-oriented process output. Supports json-rpc, plain-text, and mcp prompt styles. The daemon compiles the regex patterns at builder time and uses them at runtime to classify each incoming line as idle, generating, or an error verdict.

idlePattern.description: Regex pattern that matches a line emitted when the agent finishes a turn and is waiting for the next user message.

regex.description: ECMAScript regex source. Daemon compiles with the flags below.

description.description: Author-facing note explaining when this pattern fires.

generatingPattern.description: Regex pattern that matches a line emitted while the agent is actively working (streaming tokens, calling tools, etc.).

errorPatterns.description: List of error-signal patterns. Each entry provides a regex and the status verdict to return on match. Checked in order; first match wins.

verdict.description: Status verdict to return when this error pattern fires.

description.description: Author-facing note explaining what condition this pattern represents.

promptStyle.description: Wire format used by the agent on stdio. Affects how lines are parsed (e.g. json-rpc messages are newline-delimited JSON objects; plain-text is freeform; mcp is the Model Context Protocol framing).

oneOf.title: JSON-RPC
oneOf.description: Each line is a newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 object.

oneOf.title: Plain text
oneOf.description: Freeform text output — patterns are matched against each line directly.

oneOf.title: MCP
oneOf.description: Model Context Protocol stdio framing (Content-Length + JSON body).

messageDelimiter.description: String used to delimit messages in the stdio stream. Defaults to newline ('\n'). For MCP framing this is effectively the Content-Length header separator, but the builder uses this field to split incoming bytes into logical lines for regex matching.

idlePattern.description: Shell prompt — agent returned to idle

errorPatterns.description: Unrecoverable error — treat as idle so user can retry
